questions.author_approach: Palmgren-Miner + rainflow + Goodman mean-stress correction, then adds sliding time window (TW) to form TW-Rainflow-Goodman-Miner for real-time cumulative fatigue; compares time, RMSE/MAPE and correlation with rainflow reference.
questions.model_choice_reasoning: Retain a standard fatigue-mechanics baseline while reducing online recomputation cost; use agreement and runtime as dual criteria.
author_reported_results: CPU runtime about 0.009 s for the demonstrated calculation, under 1 s requirement
TW variant reported as closest among compared schemes by correlation/RMSE/MAPE
risks: Figure 13/14 show 10 selected turbines but prose says this validates all 100; representativeness alone is not exhaustive validation.

The printed appendix Q1 function calls MATLAB rainflow on the full prefix F(1:t,:) and does not visibly show the proposed finite sliding-window state update; the appendix as printed therefore does not by itself reproduce the claimed TW algorithm.
MAPE can become unstable when reference fatigue values are near zero; absolute and relative error should be reported together.
questions.our_assessment: Transfer the dual requirement of online speed + numerical agreement, but require boundary-sequence unit tests and an explicit streaming-state implementation. A stopwatch screenshot is supporting evidence, not a complexity proof.
alternatives: streaming/online rainflow with retained turning-point stack
incremental damage surrogate benchmarked against exact rainflow

questions.author_approach: Physics-inspired variables (tip-speed ratio, pitch angle, output/reference power) plus nonlinear regression. Compares Nelder-Mead fit with BiLSTM for shaft torque and tower thrust; body says WF1 first 70% train, last 30% test.
questions.model_choice_reasoning: Use physical variables to constrain inputs, then let a sequence model learn nonlinear residual relationships; compare against a simpler numerical-fit baseline.
author_reported_results: Table 3 reports BiLSTM R2 0.9742 for torque and 0.9854 for thrust
paper states torque MSE improvement 99.05% and thrust MSE improvement 69.35% versus Nelder-Mead
risks: Body explicitly says first 70% / last 30% temporal split, but printed MATLAB appendix executes res = res(randperm(num_samples),:) before 70/30 split. This is a paper-code evaluation mismatch and can leak future temporal regimes.
Printed code contains sequential manual-overwrite lines for torque/thrust datasets (res=...), indicating an edited/toggled script rather than a clean reproducible pipeline.
BiLSTM complexity is not justified against simpler causal baselines; a model can fit well but still be unnecessary if the relationship is mostly instantaneous.
questions.our_assessment: The strongest transferable idea is not BiLSTM itself but physics-informed feature construction + explicit simple-model competition + chronological holdout. In future time-series tasks, split first and never randomize across future samples unless stationarity is established.
alternatives: gradient boosting on lagged physical features

questions.author_approach: Two-objective fatigue minimization under power balance, per-turbine output bounds and ±1 MW deviation constraints; solved with NSGA-II/gamultiobj and compared with original/mean allocation.
questions.model_choice_reasoning: The two fatigue objectives can conflict, so a Pareto evolutionary optimizer is used rather than collapsing them a priori.
author_reported_results: aggregate power tracking error described at about 1e-7 scale for 1-100 s
text reports large fatigue reductions relative to original/mean allocation
risks: Figures 31-32 validate aggregate power balance, but aggregate balance cannot prove every turbine is within [0,5 MW] or within ±1 MW of mean allocation. The text overclaims individual-constraint verification.
One printed appendix variant returns only two total objectives but later indexes fval_before(1:num_turbines), which is structurally inconsistent as printed.

One variant simply chooses the first Pareto solution returned by gamultiobj; another selects by a summed objective. A decision rule for choosing one operational point from the Pareto set must be declared and sensitivity-tested.
Printed code variants use blade radius 63 in one place and R=40 in another, creating a parameter-consistency risk.
Using MaxTime=1 s is a compute cap, not evidence that a converged feasible Pareto solution is always found within one second.
questions.our_assessment: This is a useful counterpoint to S001 DDPG: NSGA-II gives an interpretable optimization baseline but real-time claims must report feasibility rate, Pareto-selection rule, convergence quality, and runtime distribution. Always test vector constraints directly, not through aggregate plots.
alternatives: convex/sequence quadratic approximation if a tractable surrogate exists
NSGA-II as offline gold-standard benchmark for learned policy

questions.author_approach: SVD denoising; phase-difference based delay detection; modified cubic-spline recovery; rerun Q3 optimization and compare power balance, fatigue and variance under noisy/delayed versus preprocessed data and longer horizons.
questions.model_choice_reasoning: Separate measurement corruption from optimization: clean/reconstruct signals first, then reuse the same decision model.
author_reported_results: wind-speed SNR: noisy 74.5945 dB, after SVD 77.5239 dB in Table 4
paper says 97 delayed points among 2000 and reports 3.4%, with composite difference 15.10%
multiple scenario plots report low aggregate power-balance errors
risks: 97/2000 = 4.85%, not 3.4%; basic arithmetic cross-check is required before inheriting a reported percentage.

The printed SNR code treats the FFT DC bin as signal and all other bins as noise. For a general wind-speed/time-series signal this is not a defensible SNR definition without a spectral signal band model, so the numerical SNR improvement needs independent validation.
Printed denoising code computes x_s but calls svd(Vvin), whose definition is not visible in the shown block; this prevents a clean reproduction from the appendix alone.
Figures 48-63 repeat power balance/fatigue/variance across related scenarios; the evidence can be made more compact with scenario-by-metric small multiples and a summary table.
questions.our_assessment: Transfer the staged robustness design (corruption detection → reconstruction → downstream re-evaluation), but validate the corruption detector itself and use physically meaningful SNR/error metrics. Repeated downstream plots should be consolidated while retaining a clear no-processing/noise-only/preprocessed comparison.
alternatives: cross-correlation with known timestamps for lag estimation

overall_transferable_lessons: For online engineering tasks, validate accuracy, runtime, and state-update logic separately.
For time-series prediction, preserve chronology in both prose and code; never let a random shuffle silently replace a temporal holdout.
For constrained optimization, create a constraint-by-constraint violation report instead of inferring feasibility from one aggregate equality.
For robustness, test the preprocessing metric itself before claiming downstream improvement.
Use same-problem papers as competing solution families: learned policy versus explicit Pareto optimization.
do_not_copy_blindly: random shuffle before a claimed chronological split
using total power balance to prove individual turbine constraints
arbitrary first Pareto solution as operational answer
physical constants duplicated with different values across script blocks
